probeResults: degradedArms:['party_name_disabled'], resultCount 5  =>  state 'answered', reasons [], safeForGeneration TRUE
degradedArms:['party_name_disabled'], resultCount 0  =>  state 'abstained', reasons ['low_relevance'], safeForGeneration false
degradedArms:[],                      resultCount 0  =>  state 'abstained', reasons ['low_relevance'], safeForGeneration false  <-- BYTE-IDENTICAL to the suppressed zero
whyEachIsFalse: `answered` is defined in outcome.ts as 'We searched, the arms we needed ran'. With the party arm switched off for a party_name query, that sentence is FALSE, and `safeForGeneration: true` hands that false completeness to counterarguments, briefings and drafting.
`abstained` + `low_relevance` is defined as 'The rankers ran and nothing cleared the bar'. The party arm did not run. FALSE.

A suppressed zero and an honest zero are INDISTINGUISHABLE in retrievalOutcome. That is precisely the 'there is no law on this' vs 'we could not search' collapse outcome.ts was written to end (bus 1128/1141).
observedAtHead.testCoverage: NONE. `outcome.test.ts` contains zero occurrences of 'party'. `party-search-platform.test.ts` asserts the degrade is VISIBLE in `degraded[]` and that exact identity is untouched; it asserts nothing about `retrievalOutcome`. No committed test would fail if the override were activated.

evidence: Suppression requires `partyNameArmPermitted(platform) === false`, which requires `isUserReachableOnPlatform` false, which with an empty override map and an ENABLED base cannot occur on any platform including `unknown`.

Blast radius if activated is `/search` only: `arguments/counter.ts` and `search/saved.ts` build their own `degradedArms` and never pass `partyNameArm`, so `partyArmPermitted` defaults true and they cannot suppress. They would inherit the same defect the moment either is made platform-aware.

activationGuard.scope: Adding ANY row to `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` that narrows `search.party_name` on any platform.
activationGuard.liftsWhen: ALL THREE land: (1) the contract amendment defining the new reason value; (2) the `deriveRetrievalOutcome` correction; (3) a committed test that fails if a suppressed party arm is reported as `answered` or as `abstained`/`low_relevance`.
activationGuard.note: NEW3 does not modify backend configuration and did not. This guard is a product/change-control prohibition recorded in NEW3-owned artifacts; it is not a code lock. Until the test in (3) exists, nothing in CI would catch a violation - which is the whole reason the guard is written down rather than assumed.

requiredCorrectionWhenLifted.note: Specified now so the future AMEND is mechanical. This is NOT a revision and creates none.
requiredCorrectionWhenLifted.newTopLevelState: NONE. The existing state model is preserved.
requiredCorrectionWhenLifted.newReasonValue: `arm_administratively_disabled` - added to `RetrievalOutcomeReason`. Semantics: a retrieval arm this query needed did not run because a capability was narrowed by the served registry. NOT a failure, NOT a timeout, NOT a relevance judgement, and NOT retryable.
requiredCorrectionWhenLifted.derivationChange: The suppression must join `couldNotLookProperly` in `outcome.ts`, not merely push a reason. Pushing a reason alone fixes only the non-empty case: with `resultCount === 0` the zero-result branch is reached BEFORE the reason is weighed, and the response would still read `abstained`/`low_relevance`.
resultingStates: results > 0  =>  `degraded` + `arm_administratively_disabled`  (results real, SET not known complete)
results == 0 =>  `coverage_unknown` + `arm_administratively_disabled`  (we did not look properly; may never render as 'no results')
requiredCorrectionWhenLifted.invariantSatisfied: An administratively suppressed arm becomes machine-visible in the one-place retrieval outcome, and is never explained solely as low relevance, as a timeout, or as 'all relevant rankers ran'.
requiredCorrectionWhenLifted.exactIdentityUsable: UNCHANGED - stays `true`. R14 A4.9 requires exact identity untouched, and `partySuppressed` is narrow to the `party_name` shape by construction.
requiredCorrectionWhenLifted.generationSafetyDerivation: DERIVED FROM THE EXISTING DOCUMENTED POLICY, NOT STRENGTHENED BY INTUITION. `outcome.ts` already documents `safeForGeneration` as true ONLY for `answered`, with `degraded` deliberately false because 'a partial set is safe to show and unsafe to argue from - the authority that would have changed the argument is exactly the one that did not get ranked'. A suppressed case-title probe on a party_name query is that sentence exactly. So `safeForGeneration` becomes false via the UNCHANGED existing rule, because the INPUT becomes truthful. No generation-safety policy is rewritten, no new gate is added, and the independent-sufficiency policy for other arms is untouched.
requiredCorrectionWhenLifted.wireProtocolInteger: UNCHANGED at 1. Additive within an existing open vocabulary; nothing is removed or narrowed.
